docs.text: HardFOC driver PCA9555 / PCAL9555A Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the NXP PCA9555 and PCAL9555A 16-bit I2C I/O expanders. It detects which chip is on the bus, drives and reads all sixteen pins, and uses the PCAL9555A's Agile I/O features (pull resistors, drive strength, input latch, interrupt mask and status, open-drain outputs) when they are there. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that writes and reads one register over I2C; it does the rest: variant detection, read-modify-write of the port registers, retries, interrupt decoding and error flags. 16-bit I2C GPIO expander PCA9555 / PCAL9555A NXP Semiconductors I/O 16 pins in two 8-bit ports, 5 V tolerant, 25 mA sink per pin (recommended maximum) Host interface I2C / SMBus, 0 to 400 kHz, address 0x20 to 0x27 (A2, A1, A0) Supply PCAL9555A 1.65 V to 5.5 V; PCA9555 2.3 V to 5.5 V Interrupt INT, open drain, active low; on the PCAL9555A maskable per pin, with a source register Agile I/O (PCAL9555A) Pull-up / pull-down (100 kΩ typ.), four drive levels, input latch, push-pull or open drain per port Package PCAL9555A: TSSOP24, HWQFN24; PCA9555 also SO24, SSOP24, HVQFN24. API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: bring it up, configure pins, write, read, use Agile I/O, handle interrupts and errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , with Gpio standing for pcal95555::PCAL95555<MyI2c> . The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ One PCAL95555<I2c> object per chip. Pins are numbered 0 to 15: 0-7 are P0_0 to P0_7 (port 0), 8-15 are P1_0 to P1_7 (port 1). Most settings come in three forms: Form Example Use it for One pin SetPinDirection(3, dir) One change: one register read and one write Mask SetMultipleDirections(0x00FF, dir) Many pins, one value: each port read and written once List SetDirections({{0, d0}, {8, d1}}) Many pins, different values, one pass Group Members Set-up EnsureInitialized() , GetChipVariant() , HasAgileIO() , SetRetries() , ResetToDefault() , InitFromConfig() Direction and polarity SetPinDirection() , SetMultipleDirections() , SetDirections() , SetPinPolarity() , SetMultiplePolarities() , SetPolarities() Outputs WritePin() , WritePins() , SetMultipleOutputs() , TogglePin() Inputs ReadPin() , ReadPins() , ReadAllInputs() Agile I/O (PCAL9555A) pull, drive strength, input latch, interrupt mask, SetOutputMode() Interrupts RegisterPinInterrupt() , UnregisterPinInterrupt() , SetInterruptCallback() , RegisterInterruptHandler() , HandleInterrupt() Address GetAddress() , GetAddressBits() , ChangeAddress() Raw registers ReadDualPortRegister() , WriteDualPortRegister() Errors GetErrorFlags() , HasError() , HasAnyError() , ClearError() , ClearErrorFlags() The pin enums ( GPIODir , Polarity , DriveStrength , InterruptState , InterruptEdge ), Error and the register map Pcal95555Reg are declared at global scope by pcal95555.hpp ; PCAL95555 , ChipVariant , PinReadResult and I2cInterface are in namespace pcal95555 . Bring the chip up ¶ bool bring_up ( Gpio & gpio ) { // Bus up, probe INPUT_PORT_0, detect the variant. if ( ! gpio . EnsureInitialized ()) { return false ; } const bool pcal = gpio . GetChipVariant () == ChipVariant :: PCAL9555A ; std :: printf ( "0x%02X: %s 
 " , gpio . GetAddress (), pcal ? "PCAL9555A" : "PCA9555" ); return true ; } Every call runs EnsureInitialized() on first use, so an explicit call is optional. It is the one place where a missing chip shows up as a single false instead of a failure in whichever call came first. Architecture lists what it does. Configure pins ¶ bool configure_pins ( Gpio & gpio ) { // Port 0 (pins 0-7) outputs, port 1 (pins 8-15) inputs. bool ok = gpio . SetMultipleDirections ( 0x00FF , GPIODir :: Output ); ok = ok && gpio . SetMultipleDirections ( 0xFF00 , GPIODir :: Input ); // Pins 8 and 9 are active-low buttons: invert them so a press reads as true. ok = ok && gpio . SetPolarities ({{ 8 , Polarity :: Inverted }, { 9 , Polarity :: Inverted }}); return ok ; } All pins are inputs after power-up. Polarity inversion applies to the Input Port register only: an inverted pin reads true when it is low. It does not change what an output drives. Write outputs ¶ bool drive_outputs ( Gpio & gpio ) { bool ok = gpio . WritePin ( 0 , true ); // read-modify-write ok = ok && gpio . WritePins ({{ 1 , true }, { 2 , false }}); // each port once ok = ok && gpio . SetMultipleOutputs ( 0x00F0 , false ); // pins 4-7 low ok = ok && gpio . TogglePin ( 3 ); return ok ; } WritePin() writes the Output Port register, which holds its value while the pin is an input: set the level first and then switch the direction to output to avoid a glitch. TogglePin() toggles the Output Port bit, not the measured level. Read inputs ¶ void read_inputs ( Gpio & gpio ) { const bool button = gpio . ReadPin ( 8 ); // false on a bus error too const uint16_t all = gpio . ReadAllInputs (); // bit N = pin N const auto some = gpio . ReadPins ({ 8 , 9 , 10 }); for ( const auto & [ pin , level ] : some ) { std :: printf ( "pin %u: %d 
 " , pin , level ); } if ( gpio . HasError ( Error :: I2CReadFail )) { std :: printf ( "read failed 
 " ); } ( void ) button ; ( void ) all ; } ReadPin() returns false both for a low pin and for a failed read, and ReadAllInputs() returns 0 on failure; check HasError(Error::I2CReadFail) when it matters. ReadPins() returns a PinReadResult : up to 16 (pin, level) pairs in the order you asked for them, iterable, with contains() and find() . Reading an output pin returns the level on the pin. Use Agile I/O (PCAL9555A) ¶ bool configure_agile_io ( Gpio & gpio ) { if ( ! gpio . HasAgileIO ()) { return true ; // PCA9555: none of this exists } // 100 kOhm (typ.) resistors: pin 10 pull-up, pin 11 pull-down. bool ok = gpio . SetPullEnables ({{ 10 , true }, { 11 , true }}); ok = ok && gpio . SetPullDirections ({{ 10 , true }, { 11 , false }}); // Half drive on the LED pin; port 0 open drain, port 1 push-pull. ok = ok && gpio . SetDriveStrength ( 0 , DriveStrength :: Level1 ); ok = ok && gpio . SetOutputMode ( true , false ); // Keep a short pulse on pin 12 until the input is read. ok = ok && gpio . EnableInputLatch ( 12 , true ); return ok ; } Feature Call Register Notes Pull enable SetPullEnable() 0x46 , 0x47 On at power-up; off while the port is open drain Pull direction SetPullDirection() 0x48 , 0x49 true = 100 kΩ pull-up, false = pull-down Drive strength SetDriveStrength() 0x40 to 0x43 Level0 to Level3 = 0.25 to 1 × full drive Input latch EnableInputLatch() 0x44 , 0x45 Holds a change (and its interrupt) until the read Output stage SetOutputMode() 0x4F Per port; write it before making pins outputs Interrupt mask ConfigureInterrupt() 0x4A , 0x4B All masked at power-up Check HasAgileIO() once after initialisation: on a PCA9555 these calls return false and set Error::UnsupportedFeature . PCA9555 and PCAL9555A has the full comparison. Handle interrupts ¶ bool watch_button ( Gpio & gpio ) { bool ok = gpio . SetPinDirection ( 8 , GPIODir :: Input ); ok = ok && gpio . ConfigureInterrupt ( 8 , InterruptState :: Enabled ); // PCAL9555A auto on_fall = []( uint8_t pin , bool level ) { std :: printf ( "pin %u fell, now %d 
 " , pin , level ); }; ok = ok && gpio . RegisterPinInterrupt ( 8 , InterruptEdge :: Falling , on_fall ); gpio . SetInterruptCallback ([]( uint16_t src ) { std :: printf ( "INT 0x%04X 
 " , src ); }); // The port now calls HandleInterrupt() when INT falls. return ok && gpio . RegisterInterruptHandler (); } The callbacks run in whatever context calls HandleInterrupt() : your port's interrupt task, or your polling loop. Interrupts explains the chip behaviour, the edge decoding and the pitfalls. Use several chips ¶ bool two_expanders ( MyI2c & bus ) { Gpio left ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x20 }); // A2 A1 A0 = 000 Gpio right ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x21 }); // A2 A1 A0 = 001 return left . EnsureInitialized () && right . EnsureInitialized (); } One driver object per chip, all on the same port object. Mixed PCA9555 and PCAL9555A parts on one bus are fine: each object detects its own variant. Access registers directly ¶ bool raw_registers ( Gpio & gpio ) { auto r = []( Pcal95555Reg reg ) { return static_cast < uint8_t > ( reg ); }; uint16_t config = 0 ; if ( ! gpio . ReadDualPortRegister ( r ( Pcal95555Reg :: CONFIG_PORT_0 ), r ( Pcal95555Reg :: CONFIG_PORT_1 ), config )) { return false ; } // Absolute write from a shadow you keep: no read-modify-write. return gpio . WriteDualPortRegister ( r ( Pcal95555Reg :: OUTPUT_PORT_0 ), r ( Pcal95555Reg :: OUTPUT_PORT_1 ), 0xA55A ); } ReadDualPortRegister() and WriteDualPortRegister() take the port-0 and port-1 command bytes and move a 16-bit value with bit N = pin N. WriteDualPortRegister() writes without reading first, which suits code that keeps its own shadow of the Output or Configuration registers. They do not check the Agile I/O guard: on a PCA9555 a command from 0x40 up NACKs and sets the I2C error flag. Handle errors ¶ void report_errors ( Gpio & gpio ) { if ( ! gpio . HasAnyError ()) { return ; } if ( gpio . HasError ( Error :: I2CReadFail ) || gpio . HasError ( Error :: I2CWriteFail )) { std :: printf ( "bus: NACK or timeout at 0x%02X 
 " , gpio . GetAddress ()); } if ( gpio . HasError ( Error :: UnsupportedFeature )) { std :: printf ( "Agile I/O call on a PCA9555 
 " ); } if ( gpio . HasError ( Error :: InvalidPin )) { std :: printf ( "pin index above 15 
 " ); } // Sticky until cleared, or until a later success clears its own flag. gpio . ClearErrorFlags (); } Flag Set when Cleared by Error::I2CReadFail A register read failed after all retries, or initialisation found no chip The next successful read Error::I2CWriteFail A register write failed after all retries The next successful write Error::InvalidPin A pin above 15 The next call with a valid pin Error::UnsupportedFeature An Agile I/O call on a PCA9555 (or an undetected variant) ClearError() / ClearErrorFlags() Error::InvalidAddress ChangeAddress(address) outside 0x20 to 0x27 A successful ChangeAddress() Error::InvalidMask Declared; no call sets it at present GetErrorFlags() returns the flags as a uint16_t ; HasError() tests one, ClearErrorFlags(mask) clears the bits in mask (all by default). Restore defaults ¶ ResetToDefault() writes the power-up values of every register (the Agile I/O bank too on a PCAL9555A), since the chips have no reset pin. Configuration covers InitFromConfig() and the retry count.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: three layers, what each owns, and how one call reaches the chip. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one PCAL95555 object per chip. The core owns the chip's register map (listed from Pcal95555Reg in inc/pcal95555.hpp): the eight standard registers both chips have, and the Agile I/O bank only the PCAL9555A answers, which the driver guards after it has detected the variant. The communication interface (pcal95555::I2cInterface in inc/pcal95555_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: three methods are required, the rest have defaults. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the chip. Drawn from: inc/pcal95555.hpp Pcal95555Reg ; inc/pcal95555_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The three layers ¶ Layer Where You change it when Core : PCAL95555<I2c> pcal95555.hpp , pcal95555.ipp Never, for a new board Interface : I2cInterface<Self> pcal95555_i2c_interface.hpp Never Port : your class, over your SDK Your project Once per MCU or board ( Porting ) The core depends only on the interface's methods, and the interface only on three methods of your port. Everything above the port is the same on ESP32, STM32, a Linux host or the unit-test model. That is how the host tests run the real driver code without hardware. How one call reaches the chip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant D as PCAL95555 core participant P as Your port participant C as PCAL9555A A->>D: WritePin(9, false) D->>D: EnsureInitialized() (first call only) D->>D: pin 9: port 1, bit 1 D->>P: Read(0x20, OUTPUT_PORT_1) P->>C: W 0x03, Sr, R 1 byte C-->>P: 0xFF P-->>D: true D->>P: Write(0x20, OUTPUT_PORT_1, 0xFD) P->>C: W 0x03 0xFD C-->>P: ACK P-->>D: true D-->>A: true (clears I2CWriteFail) A failed transfer is retried SetRetries() times (once by default) before the call returns false and sets Error::I2CReadFail or Error::I2CWriteFail . What happens at initialisation ¶ Construction does no I/O. The first call that needs the chip, or your own EnsureInitialized() , runs: EnsureInitialized() on your port: bring the bus up. SetAddressPins() on your port, which may drive A2-A0 (the default does nothing). A read of Input Port 0 at the address: if it fails, I2CReadFail is set and the call returns false . Variant detection, unless the constructor fixed the variant: read Input Port 0, read Output Port Configuration (0x4F) without retries, read Input Port 0 again. An ACK at 0x4F means PCAL9555A; a NACK followed by a good read means PCA9555. See PCA9555 and PCAL9555A . A snapshot of both input ports, the reference for edge detection. Why CRTP ¶ The interface is a class template parameter, not a virtual base class. The compiler sees your port's methods directly and inlines them; the driver has no vtable and needs no RTTI. The cost is that the driver type names the port: PCAL95555<MyI2c> . Code that has to work with several port types takes the driver as a template parameter too. The optional methods ( SetAddressPins() , RegisterInterruptHandler() , GpioSet() , GpioRead() ) have bodies in the base class. A port that declares a method with the same name hides the default; the driver always calls through the port type, so the port's version is the one that runs. Design choices ¶ Read-modify-write on single registers. Single-pin calls read the port's register, change one bit and write it back: two transactions. Mask and list calls read both ports once and write each once. One register per transaction. No paired or auto-increment transfers, so any I2C controller that can do a register read can run the driver ( Hardware ). Sticky error flags. Calls return bool ; the flags say why, and stay set until cleared or until a later success of the same kind clears its own flag. Static staging bytes. Register transfers go through function-local static buffers, kept in internal RAM for MCUs whose I2C DMA cannot reach the stack. As a consequence, two driver objects must not run calls at the same time from different threads (see Porting ). docs.text: Configuration ¶ What you can set before and at start-up: the address and variant, retries, the power-up state and the compile-time pin configuration that InitFromConfig() applies. Address and variant ¶ Both constructors take the I2C port by pointer and an optional pcal95555::ChipVariant : Constructor Address PCAL95555(bus, a0, a1, a2, variant = Unknown) 0x20 + (a2 << 2 | a1 << 1 | a0) PCAL95555(bus, uint8_t address, variant = Unknown) address , clamped to 0x20 to 0x27 without an error // Skip auto-detection when the board fixes the part. void make_drivers ( MyI2c & bus ) { using pcal95555 :: ChipVariant ; Gpio auto_detect ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x20 }); // probes 0x4F once Gpio known_pcal ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x21 }, ChipVariant :: PCAL9555A ); Gpio known_pca ( & bus , true , true , false , ChipVariant :: PCA9555 ); // 0x23 ( void ) auto_detect ; ( void ) known_pcal ; ( void ) known_pca ; } Unknown (the default) runs the detection probe described in PCA9555 and PCAL9555A . Start-up sequence ¶ bool apply_startup_config ( Gpio & gpio ) { gpio . SetRetries ( 2 ); // each register access tries up to 3 times gpio . ResetToDefault (); // datasheet power-up values (both banks on a PCAL9555A) gpio . InitFromConfig (); // then the CONFIG_PCAL95555_* values return ! gpio . HasAnyError (); } Call Effect SetRetries(n) Each register access is tried n + 1 times before it fails; default n = 1 . The detection probe always runs without retries ResetToDefault() Writes the datasheet power-up value of every register: outputs high, no inversion, all inputs; on a PCAL9555A also full drive, no latch, pull-ups on, interrupts masked, push-pull InitFromConfig() Writes the compile-time configuration below: Output Port and Configuration registers; on a PCAL9555A also pull enable, pull select and output mode. Does nothing when CONFIG_PCAL95555_INIT_FROM_KCONFIG is 0 Compile-time pin configuration ¶ InitFromConfig() reads CONFIG_PCAL95555_* macros. inc/pcal95555_kconfig.hpp defines every one that is not already defined, and the Kconfig file at the repository root describes the same options as an ESP-IDF menu. Macro Default Meaning CONFIG_PCAL95555_INIT_FROM_KCONFIG 1 InitFromConfig() applies the values below; 0 makes it a no-op CONFIG_PCAL95555_Pp_n_DIR 1 Pin Pp_n is an input ( 1 ) or output ( 0 ) CONFIG_PCAL95555_Pp_n_OUTPUT 0 Initial output level CONFIG_PCAL95555_Pp_n_PULL 0 Pull resistor enabled (PCAL9555A) CONFIG_PCAL95555_Pp_n_PULL_UP 1 Pull-up ( 1 ) or pull-down ( 0 ) (PCAL9555A) CONFIG_PCAL95555_PORT0_OD , CONFIG_PCAL95555_PORT1_OD 0 Port in open-drain mode (PCAL9555A) p is the port (0 or 1) and n the pin (0 to 7), for example CONFIG_PCAL95555_P1_3_DIR . The header combines them into 16-bit values ( CONFIG_PCAL95555_INIT_DIRECTION , _INIT_OUTPUT , _INIT_PULL_ENABLE , _INIT_PULL_UP ) that you can also define directly, for example with target_compile_definitions() . The defaults are not the power-up state With every macro at its default, InitFromConfig() drives all outputs low in the Output Port register and, on a PCAL9555A, disables every pull resistor (the chip powers up with pull-ups on). Define the macros you need before calling it, or call only ResetToDefault() . ESP-IDF menuconfig The ESP-IDF component wrapper in examples/esp32/components/hf_pcal95555/ does not include the root Kconfig , so idf.py menuconfig does not show these options and sdkconfig does not define them. Until it does, set the macros with compile definitions. CONFIG_PCAL95555_DEFAULT_ADDRESS in Kconfig is not read by the driver. Run-time settings ¶ Everything else (directions, polarity, pulls, drive strength, latch, output mode, interrupt mask) is a run-time call; the API guide shows each one. Recommended settings by pin use: Pin use PCA9555 PCAL9555A Push button to ground Input; external pull-up if the line is long Input, pull-up (power-up default), latch if presses are short LED to VDD (sinking) Output, high = off Output, drive Level3 (power-up default) Shared or wired-OR line Not possible: push-pull only SetOutputMode() open drain for that port, then output Interrupt input Input Input, then ConfigureInterrupt(pin, InterruptState::Enabled) Next: Porting .

docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between your MCU and a PCA9555 or PCAL9555A, with which bus settings, and the limits that matter to the host. All values here come from the PCAL9555A datasheet (Rev. 2, December 2014) and the PCA9555 datasheet (Rev. 10, November 2017). When they disagree with a board's schematic, the schematic wins for pin numbers. Pins ¶ The two parts are pin-compatible in the same package: a PCAL9555A drops into a PCA9555 footprint. Signal TSSOP24 pin HWQFN24 pin Direction (chip) Notes INT 1 22 out, open drain Active low; pull it up to the MCU's I/O voltage A1, A2 2, 3 23, 24 in Address bits; tie to VDD or VSS P0_0 to P0_7 4 to 11 1 to 8 in / out Driver pins 0 to 7 (port 0) VSS 12 9 and exposed pad power Connect the pin, not only the pad P1_0 to P1_7 13 to 20 10 to 17 in / out Driver pins 8 to 15 (port 1) A0 21 18 in Address bit 0 SCL 22 19 in I2C clock SDA 23 20 in / out, open drain I2C data VDD 24 21 power Decouple with 100 nF close to the pin Neither part has a reset pin: only a power cycle below the power-on-reset threshold resets the registers. ResetToDefault() writes the power-up values instead. The NXP datasheet of the PCA9555 names the port pins IO0_0 to IO1_7; they are the same pins. Address ¶ The 7-bit address is 0100 A2 A1 A0 : 0x20 to 0x27, up to eight expanders on one bus, in any mix of PCA9555 and PCAL9555A. A2 A1 A0 Address 0 0 0 0x20 0 0 1 0x21 0 1 0 0x22 0 1 1 0x23 1 0 0 0x24 1 0 1 0x25 1 1 0 0x26 1 1 1 0x27 The driver takes either the three pin levels or the address. A board that drives A2-A0 from MCU GPIOs can move a chip at run time with ChangeAddress() , through the port's optional SetAddressPins() . Bus settings ¶ Setting Value Bus I2C / SMBus, 7-bit address Clock 0 to 400 kHz (Standard mode and Fast mode); no Fast-mode Plus Register access [address+W] [command] [data] to write; [address+W] [command] Sr [address+R] [data] to read Register pairs After each byte the command toggles between the two registers of a pair (port 0 / port 1) Input levels (SCL, SDA, A0-A2, P ports) V IH ≥ 0.7 × VDD, V IL ≤ 0.3 × VDD; inputs tolerate 5.5 V Spike filter 50 ns on SCL and SDA The driver sends one register per transaction, even for pairs: a two-byte paired write was seen to leave the Configuration registers wrong behind one I2C controller. Your port therefore never needs more than a 2-byte write (command and data) and a 1-byte read. sequenceDiagram participant H as Host (driver) participant C as PCA9555 / PCAL9555A H->>C: START, 0x20+W, command 0x03 (Output port 1) C-->>H: ACK H->>C: data byte C-->>H: ACK, STOP: outputs change within tv(Q) H->>C: START, 0x20+W, command 0x01 (Input port 1) C-->>H: ACK H->>C: repeated START, 0x20+R C-->>H: input byte, INT released (the read clears the interrupt) Timing that affects the host ¶ Parameter PCAL9555A PCA9555 Meaning t v(Q) 400 ns max 200 ns max Output valid after the ACK of the data byte t v(INT) 1 µs max 4 µs max INT asserted after an input changes t rst(INT) 1 µs max 4 µs max INT released after the Input Port read INT goes active when an input differs from the Input Port register's last read value (on the PCAL9555A only for unmasked pins) and goes inactive when that port is read, or when the input returns to its old level first (unless it is latched). Interrupts shows how the driver turns that into per-pin callbacks. Power and drive ¶ Quantity PCAL9555A PCA9555 VDD 1.65 V to 5.5 V 2.3 V to 5.5 V Supply current, inputs, 400 kHz bus 10 µA typ., 25 µA max (VDD 3.6 V to 5.5 V) 135 µA typ., 200 µA max (5.5 V, 100 kHz) Sink current per pin (recommended) 25 mA max 25 mA max (limit externally) Source current per pin (recommended) 10 mA max V OH specified at 8 and 10 mA Total through VSS 200 mA max 200 mA max (100 mA per port) Internal pull 100 kΩ typ. (50 to 150 kΩ), up or down, per pin, on by default (pull-up) Weak pull-up (about 100 kΩ) on every input, always on Operating temperature -40 °C to +85 °C -40 °C to +85 °C On the PCAL9555A the drive strength sets how much of the full output current a pin can sink or source: Level0 to Level3 are 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1 times full drive. Lower levels slow the edges and cut ground bounce in low-capacitance loads; they are not a current limit for LEDs. Set open drain before making pins outputs The PCAL9555A datasheet recommends writing the Output port configuration register (0x4F) before the Configuration registers turn pins into outputs. Call SetOutputMode() before SetPinDirection(pin, GPIODir::Output) on a port that shares a line with other drivers. A PCA9555 has push-pull outputs only. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake or ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 12+ or a current MSVC. No RTOS or exceptions. Every call except RegisterPinInterrupt() is noexcept and returns bool , a value or sets an error flag. The driver keeps std::function callbacks, so registering a callback may allocate. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-pcal95555-driver.git external/hf-pcal95555-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-pcal95555-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. CMake ¶ add_subdirectory ( external/hf-pcal95555-driver ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE hf::pcal95555 ) hf::pcal95555 is an alias of the hf_pcal95555 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories ( inc/ and the generated version header) and requires C++20 ( cxx_std_20 ), so your target does not need to set either. find_package(hf_pcal95555) works after cmake --install . Option Default Effect HF_PCAL95555_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on targets that link the driver HF_PCAL95555_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host unit tests in tests/ ( Testing and CI ) ESP-IDF ¶ The ESP-IDF component wrapper is examples/esp32/components/hf_pcal95555/ . Copy that folder into your project's components/ (or point EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS at it) and set the HF_PCAL95555_ROOT cache variable to the driver checkout; the wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_pcal95555 . The wrapper requires the IDF driver component, which the ESP32 reference port uses. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_pcal95555_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, install and package export ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_pcal95555/CMakeLists.txt IDF component wrapper over the same settings The version is set once in the settings file and written into pcal95555_version.h at configure time. Read it at compile or run time: const char * v = pcal95555 :: PCAL95555 < MyI2c >:: GetDriverVersion (); // "1.0.0" Compile-time configuration ¶ inc/pcal95555_kconfig.hpp gives every CONFIG_PCAL95555_* macro a default, so the driver builds without ESP-IDF. The values only matter to InitFromConfig() ; Configuration lists them. Next ¶ Quickstart wires the chip and lights an LED; Porting writes the I2C interface for your MCU.

docs.text: Interrupts ¶ How the chips signal an input change on INT, how the driver turns that into per-pin callbacks, and what you must do in your port and your application. What the chip does ¶ INT is an open-drain, active-low output. It goes active when an input pin differs from the value the Input Port register held when it was last read. It goes inactive when the host reads the Input Port register of that port, or when the input returns to its earlier level before the read. Behaviour PCA9555 PCAL9555A Pins that can raise INT Every pin configured as an input Inputs whose INT_MASK bit is 0 Interrupt mask at power-up none (all inputs active) all masked ( 0xFF , 0xFF ) Which pin changed Compare two Input Port reads INT_STATUS_0 , INT_STATUS_1 : 1 = source Cleared by Reading the Input Port register Reading the Input Port register (reading the status does not clear it) Short pulses Lost if the pin returns before the read Kept with the input latch ( EnableInputLatch() ) until the read What the driver does ¶ HandleInterrupt() is the whole interrupt path: Find the sources: on a PCAL9555A, read INT_STATUS_0 and INT_STATUS_1 ; on a PCA9555, read both Input Port registers and XOR them with the previous snapshot. Read both Input Port registers. This also clears INT. Call the global callback ( SetInterruptCallback() ) with the 16-bit source mask. For every source pin with a callback ( RegisterPinInterrupt() ), compare the previous and current level and call the callback if the edge matches InterruptEdge::Rising , Falling or Both . Store the current levels as the new snapshot. HandleInterrupt() does I2C transfers, so it must run in a task, never in an interrupt service routine. Set it up ¶ bool watch_button ( Gpio & gpio ) { bool ok = gpio . SetPinDirection ( 8 , GPIODir :: Input ); ok = ok && gpio . ConfigureInterrupt ( 8 , InterruptState :: Enabled ); // PCAL9555A auto on_fall = []( uint8_t pin , bool level ) { std :: printf ( "pin %u fell, now %d \n " , pin , level ); }; ok = ok && gpio . RegisterPinInterrupt ( 8 , InterruptEdge :: Falling , on_fall ); gpio . SetInterruptCallback ([]( uint16_t src ) { std :: printf ( "INT 0x%04X \n " , src ); }); // The port now calls HandleInterrupt() when INT falls. return ok && gpio . RegisterInterruptHandler (); } RegisterInterruptHandler() hands a closure that calls HandleInterrupt() to your port's optional RegisterInterruptHandler(std::function<void()>) . A port that supports it attaches a falling-edge interrupt on the MCU pin wired to INT and runs the closure from a task when it fires; the ESP32 port does this with a GPIO ISR that wakes a FreeRTOS task. If your port keeps the default, RegisterInterruptHandler() returns false and you call the handler yourself. Poll instead ¶ void poll_for_changes ( Gpio & gpio ) { // No INT line, or a port without RegisterInterruptHandler(): call it yourself. // Reads the sources (PCAL9555A) or diffs the inputs (PCA9555), then calls back. gpio . HandleInterrupt (); } Without an INT line, call HandleInterrupt() from a periodic task. On a PCA9555 that is change detection by polling; on a PCAL9555A it also picks up latched inputs that changed between polls. Pitfalls ¶ Symptom Cause Fix No interrupt at all on a PCAL9555A Every pin is masked at power-up ConfigureInterrupt(pin, InterruptState::Enabled) INT stays low Nobody reads the Input Port register Make sure HandleInterrupt() runs; any ReadPin() of that port also clears it A PCAL9555A callback is missed Another call read the Input Port between the change and the handler, which cleared the interrupt before the handler saw it Let the handler be the only reader of interrupt inputs, and use the callback's level argument Fast pulses are missed The input returned before the read PCAL9555A: EnableInputLatch(pin, true) RegisterPinInterrupt() returns false Pin above 15, an empty callback, or initialisation failed Check the pin and GetErrorFlags() Next: API guide .

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the I2C communication interface. The driver never calls your SDK directly. It calls a few methods on a class you derive from pcal95555::I2cInterface<Self> (in inc/pcal95555_i2c_interface.hpp ). The base class uses CRTP: the calls are resolved at compile time, so there are no virtual functions and no vtable. Three layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application talks to one PCAL95555 object per chip. The core owns the chip's register map (listed from Pcal95555Reg in inc/pcal95555.hpp): the eight standard registers both chips have, and the Agile I/O bank only the PCAL9555A answers, which the driver guards after it has detected the variant. The communication interface (pcal95555::I2cInterface in inc/pcal95555_i2c_interface.hpp) is a CRTP base: three methods are required, the rest have defaults. The platform port is the only code you write. Below it is the chip. Drawn from: inc/pcal95555.hpp Pcal95555Reg ; inc/pcal95555_i2c_interface.hpp I2cInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract EnsureInitialized() yes Bring the bus up on the first call, return true at once afterwards. false stops initialisation with I2CReadFail Write(addr, reg, data, len) yes One transaction: START, addr + W, reg , len data bytes, STOP. The driver always passes len = 1 . Return false on a NACK or timeout Read(addr, reg, data, len) yes Write reg , repeated START, read len bytes, STOP. The driver always passes len = 1 . Return false on a NACK or timeout SetAddressPins(a0, a1, a2) no Drive A0-A2 from MCU GPIOs, if the board wires them; the default returns false RegisterInterruptHandler(handler) no Keep handler and run it from a task when INT falls; the default returns false GpioSet(pin, signal) , GpioRead(pin, signal) no Control-pin hooks of the HardFOC interface model; this driver does not call them, since neither chip has a reset pin addr is the 7-bit address (0x20 to 0x27); your SDK may want it shifted left by one. The port ¶ my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public pcal95555 :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : // Bring the bus up once; the driver calls this before its first transfer. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One register write: [addr+W] [reg] [data...] STOP. Return false on a NACK. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 3 ] = { reg , 0 , 0 }; if ( len > 2 ) { return false ; // the driver writes one register at a time } for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < len ; ++ i ) { frame [ 1 + i ] = data [ i ]; } return platform_i2c_write ( addr , frame , 1 + len ); } // One register read: [addr+W] [reg] repeated START [addr+R] [data...] STOP. bool Read ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , & reg , 1 , data , len ); } // Optional: keep the driver's interrupt handler. Without it, poll instead. bool RegisterInterruptHandler ( std :: function < void () > handler ) noexcept { handler_ = std :: move ( handler ); return true ; } // Call from a task, not from the ISR, after INT (open drain, active low) falls: // the handler reads the chip over I2C. void ServiceInterrupt () { if ( handler_ ) { handler_ (); } } private : bool ready_ = false ; std :: function < void () > handler_ ; }; Rules the transfers must follow: Return false for a NACK. Variant detection depends on it: a PCA9555 NACKs command 0x4F, and a port that reports success anyway makes the driver believe it talks to a PCAL9555A. Recover after a NACK. The next transfer must work. Some controllers need a bus reset after a NACK; do it inside Read() / Write() . Repeated START for reads. The chips also accept a STOP between the command and the read, but a repeated start keeps another master from slipping in between. Bounded time. Use a timeout (a few milliseconds is plenty at 100 or 400 kHz); a stuck bus must not block forever. Interrupt support ¶ RegisterInterruptHandler() receives a closure that calls the driver's HandleInterrupt() , which does I2C. Run it from a task, not from the ISR: the usual pattern is an ISR on the INT pin's falling edge that wakes a task, which calls the closure. Configure the MCU pin as an input with a pull-up (or rely on an external one); INT is open drain. Reference implementation ¶ The ESP32 examples use esp32_pcal95555_bus.hpp : an ESP-IDF i2c_master port at 400 kHz with internal pull-ups, GPIO-driven A0-A2 and an INT ISR that wakes a FreeRTOS task. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the port on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over it. Call EnsureInitialized() and print GetChipVariant() : it must match the part marking. Toggle an output with TogglePin() and watch it with a meter or a logic analyser. Read GetErrorFlags() after a few hundred calls: it should stay 0 on a healthy bus. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe, and register transfers share function-local static buffers across all driver objects of the same port type. Give every expander on a port type one owner task, or guard every driver call with one mutex shared by all of them. Callbacks run in the task that calls HandleInterrupt() .

docs.text: RegisterInterruptHandler() receives a closure that calls the driver's HandleInterrupt() , which does I2C. Run it from a task, not from the ISR: the usual pattern is an ISR on the INT pin's falling edge that wakes a task, which calls the closure. Configure the MCU pin as an input with a pull-up (or rely on an external one); INT is open drain.

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe, and register transfers share function-local static buffers across all driver objects of the same port type. Wire it ¶ MCU PCA9555 / PCAL9555A Notes I2C SCL SCL Pull-up to the bus voltage (4.7 kΩ is a common value at 400 kHz) I2C SDA SDA Pull-up as for SCL GND VSS Common ground 3.3 V VDD 1.65 V to 5.5 V (PCAL9555A) or 2.3 V to 5.5 V (PCA9555); 100 nF next to the pin GND A0, A1, A2 Address 0x20; tie each pin to VDD or VSS, never leave it open GPIO in (optional) INT Open drain, active low: pull it up For the example, connect an LED with a series resistor from P0_0 (pin 0) to VDD, so the expander sinks its current, and a push button from P1_0 (pin 8) to ground. The Hardware page has the pin numbers per package, the address table and the electrical limits. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and link the hf_pcal95555 CMake target (or add inc/ to your include path and build with C++20). Installation covers CMake and ESP-IDF. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-pcal95555-driver.git external/hf-pcal95555-driver 3. Write the port ¶ The port is the only platform code. Replace the platform_* calls with your SDK's. my_i2c.hpp class MyI2c : public pcal95555 :: I2cInterface < MyI2c > { public : // Bring the bus up once; the driver calls this before its first transfer. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_i2c_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One register write: [addr+W] [reg] [data...] STOP. Return false on a NACK. bool Write ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , const uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { uint8_t frame [ 3 ] = { reg , 0 , 0 }; if ( len > 2 ) { return false ; // the driver writes one register at a time } for ( size_t i = 0 ; i < len ; ++ i ) { frame [ 1 + i ] = data [ i ]; } return platform_i2c_write ( addr , frame , 1 + len ); } // One register read: [addr+W] [reg] repeated START [addr+R] [data...] STOP. bool Read ( uint8_t addr , uint8_t reg , uint8_t * data , size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_i2c_write_read ( addr , & reg , 1 , data , len ); } // Optional: keep the driver's interrupt handler. EnsureInitialized ()) { // 1. probe, detect the variant return -1 ; // wiring, pull-ups or address } gpio . SetPinDirection ( 0 , GPIODir :: Output ); // 2. P0_0 drives an LED gpio . SetPinDirection ( 8 , GPIODir :: Input ); // P1_0 reads a button const bool pressed = ! gpio . ReadPin ( 8 ); // 3. button pulls the pin low if ( ! gpio . WritePin ( 0 , pressed )) { // 4. docs.text: PCA9555 and PCAL9555A ¶ What the two parts have in common, what only the PCAL9555A adds, and how the driver tells them apart. The PCAL9555A is a pin-to-pin and software-compatible successor of the PCA9555: it has the PCA9555's eight registers at the same command bytes, and a second bank of Agile I/O registers at 0x40 to 0x4F. Code written for the PCA9555 runs unchanged on a PCAL9555A. Two power-up differences matter: the PCAL9555A starts with every interrupt masked, and with 100 kΩ pull-ups enabled. Features by part ¶ Feature PCA9555 PCAL9555A Driver calls Direction, output, input, polarity inversion yes yes SetPinDirection() , WritePin() , ReadPin() , SetPinPolarity() and their mask / list forms INT output on input change yes, every input yes, unmasked inputs HandleInterrupt() , RegisterPinInterrupt() Interrupt mask per pin yes ConfigureInterrupt() , ConfigureInterrupts() , ConfigureInterruptMask() Interrupt source register yes GetInterruptStatus() Pull-up or pull-down per pin (100 kΩ typ.) fixed weak pull-up yes SetPullEnable() , SetPullDirection() , GetPullConfiguration() and list forms Output drive strength, 4 levels per pin yes SetDriveStrength() , SetDriveStrengths() Input latch per pin yes EnableInputLatch() , EnableMultipleInputLatches() , EnableInputLatches() Push-pull or open drain per port push-pull yes SetOutputMode() Supply range 2.3 V to 5.5 V 1.65 V to 5.5 V On a PCA9555 every call in the PCAL9555A-only rows returns false (or 0 for GetInterruptStatus() ), sets Error::UnsupportedFeature and sends nothing on the bus. Register map ¶ Command Register Default Part 0x00 , 0x01 INPUT_PORT_0 , INPUT_PORT_1 (read only) pins both 0x02 , 0x03 OUTPUT_PORT_0 , OUTPUT_PORT_1 0xFF both 0x04 , 0x05 POLARITY_INV_0 , POLARITY_INV_1 0x00 both 0x06 , 0x07 CONFIG_PORT_0 , CONFIG_PORT_1 (1 = input) 0xFF both 0x40 to 0x43 DRIVE_STRENGTH_0 to _3 0xFF PCAL9555A 0x44 , 0x45 INPUT_LATCH_0 , INPUT_LATCH_1 0x00 PCAL9555A 0x46 , 0x47 PULL_ENABLE_0 , PULL_ENABLE_1 0xFF PCAL9555A 0x48 , 0x49 PULL_SELECT_0 , PULL_SELECT_1 (1 = pull-up) 0xFF PCAL9555A 0x4A , 0x4B INT_MASK_0 , INT_MASK_1 (1 = masked) 0xFF PCAL9555A 0x4C , 0x4D INT_STATUS_0 , INT_STATUS_1 (read only) 0x00 PCAL9555A 0x4F OUTPUT_CONF ( ODEN1 , ODEN0 ) 0x00 PCAL9555A The names are the Pcal95555Reg enumerators. The drive-strength registers hold four pins each: 0x40 pins 0-3, 0x41 pins 4-7, 0x42 pins 8-11, 0x43 pins 12-15, two bits per pin from bit 0 up ( 00 = 0.25, 11 = full). How the driver detects the part ¶ flowchart TD A[Read INPUT_PORT_0] -->|NACK| U[Unknown: bus or address problem] A -->|ACK| B[Read OUTPUT_CONF 0x4F, no retries] B -->|ACK| P[PCAL9555A] B -->|NACK| C[Read INPUT_PORT_0 again] C -->|ACK| S[PCA9555] C -->|NACK| U The detection relies on a PCA9555 not acknowledging command byte 0x4F. The PCA9555 datasheet defines only commands 0x00 to 0x07 and does not say how the chip answers others, so treat the result as a well-tested heuristic, not a guarantee. If your board fixes the part, pass the variant to the constructor and the probe is skipped: // Skip auto-detection when the board fixes the part. void make_drivers ( MyI2c & bus ) { using pcal95555 :: ChipVariant ; Gpio auto_detect ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x20 }); // probes 0x4F once Gpio known_pcal ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x21 }, ChipVariant :: PCAL9555A ); Gpio known_pca ( & bus , true , true , false , ChipVariant :: PCA9555 ); // 0x23 ( void ) auto_detect ; ( void ) known_pcal ; ( void ) known_pca ; } Unknown after initialisation When the second read of Input Port 0 also fails, detection leaves ChipVariant::Unknown , EnsureInitialized() still returns true and every Agile I/O call fails with UnsupportedFeature . Check GetChipVariant() after bring-up, and fix the bus ( Troubleshooting ) or pass the variant explicitly. Porting PCA9555 code to a PCAL9555A ¶ Interrupts: unmask the pins you want with ConfigureInterrupt(pin, InterruptState::Enabled) . A PCA9555 needs nothing; a PCAL9555A raises no interrupt until you do. Pull-ups: the PCAL9555A enables a 100 kΩ pull-up on every pin at power-up. Disable it ( SetPullEnable(pin, false) ) on pins with an external pull-down or an analogue load. Nothing else changes: same address range, same pins, same eight registers. Next: Interrupts .

docs.text: flowchart TD A[Read INPUT_PORT_0] -->|NACK| U[Unknown: bus or address problem] A -->|ACK| B[Read OUTPUT_CONF 0x4F, no retries] B -->|ACK| P[PCAL9555A] B -->|NACK| C[Read INPUT_PORT_0 again] C -->|ACK| S[PCA9555] C -->|NACK| U The detection relies on a PCA9555 not acknowledging command byte 0x4F. The PCA9555 datasheet defines only commands 0x00 to 0x07 and does not say how the chip answers others, so treat the result as a well-tested heuristic, not a guarantee. If your board fixes the part, pass the variant to the constructor and the probe is skipped: // Skip auto-detection when the board fixes the part. void make_drivers ( MyI2c & bus ) { using pcal95555 :: ChipVariant ; Gpio auto_detect ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x20 }); // probes 0x4F once Gpio known_pcal ( & bus , uint8_t { 0x21 }, ChipVariant :: PCAL9555A ); Gpio known_pca ( & bus , true , true , false , ChipVariant :: PCA9555 ); // 0x23 ( void ) auto_detect ; ( void ) known_pcal ; ( void ) known_pca ; } Unknown after initialisation When the second read of Input Port 0 also fails, detection leaves ChipVariant::Unknown , EnsureInitialized() still returns true and every Agile I/O call fails with UnsupportedFeature . Check GetChipVariant() after bring-up, and fix the bus ( Troubleshooting ) or pass the variant explicitly.

docs.text: Interrupts: unmask the pins you want with ConfigureInterrupt(pin, InterruptState::Enabled) . A PCA9555 needs nothing; a PCAL9555A raises no interrupt until you do. Pull-ups: the PCAL9555A enables a 100 kΩ pull-up on every pin at power-up. Disable it ( SetPullEnable(pin, false) ) on pins with an external pull-down or an analogue load. Nothing else changes: same address range, same pins, same eight registers. Next: Interrupts .
